content:
lina: FYI escalated from support: acme-inc seeing sustained Dedicated throttling even though they have a gold reservation. They say requests are hitting gpu-small-1 and getting 429s. customer-provided sample request IDs: rq_8a1f2, rq_8a1f9.

alex: Confirming — our app started getting 429s around 09:12 UTC. We pinned to model rwd-3b and set tier header to 'gold'. Traffic should have gone to gold-dedicated-01. Logs show pool=gpu-small-1 in response.

lina: attaching snippets pasted from their controlplane trace (redacted tenant):
```
route_decision: {request_id: rq_8a1f2, tenant: acme, headers: {x-tier: "silver", x-tenant-tier: "gold"}, selected_pool: gpu-small-1, reason: "tier_match: x-tier"}
route_decision: {request_id: rq_8a1f9, tenant: acme, headers: {x-tier: "silver"}, selected_pool: gpu-small-1}
```

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-3124, severity=high, owners=@devon,@maya :rotating_light:

devon: looking — this smells like header precedence. We recently applied the tierkey parser change last week. Lina, can you paste the full raw headers from one of the failing requests (including duplicates)? Also need controlplane logs around decision time (debug routing).

alex: here's a raw capture (sanitized):
```
GET /v1/generate
Host: inference.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
x-tenant-id: acme
x-tenant-tier: gold
x-tier: silver
User-Agent: acme-prod/1.2.3
X-Request-Id: rq_8a1f2
```

devon: thanks. Repro idea: if parser now prefers x-tier over x-tenant-tier (top-level key), it would shadow tenant-specific tier, causing tenant traffic to land on lower pool. That would explain throttling.

maya: confirm — controlplane change CP-4452 (tierkey normalization) collapsed multiple tier keys and we adjusted precedence to prefer canonical 'tier' header. That unintentionally made 'x-tier' dominant over 'x-tenant-tier' when both present. We introduced a regression for customers passing tenant-scoped tier headers.

qa-sam: I ran a quick local repro: with two headers present the decision log shows same behavior: selected_pool switches to small when x-tier=silver even if x-tenant-tier=gold. Repro steps:
1) curl -v -H "x-tenant-id: acme" -H "x-tenant-tier: gold" -H "x-tier: silver" \"https://staging.inference/...\"
2) watch controlplane debug logs for request_id
Result: selected_pool=gpu-small-1.

lina: customer impact: their gold reserved throughput capped, some requests failed with 429, billing unaffected but SLAs violated. They want mitigation ASAP.

devon: immediate mitigation options:
- hotfix: revert CP-4452 precedence change (quick rollback) => likely to restore previous routing.
- short-term workaround: add config in tenant routing to ignore top-level x-tier if x-tenant-tier present (per-tenant rule) => requires controlplane config deploy but lower blast radius.

maya: I'll push revert PR now to staging and run canary. If green, push to prod. Also will add an explicit precedence test in unit/regression suite.

devon: once revert is live, we should notify acme and check request ids from their window to confirm retroactive corrections for routing? note: routing decisions are not retroactive, but traffic should stop misrouting.

alex: thanks. Can you confirm ETA for rollback? Our customer is asking for timeline.

maya: ETA ~45m for staged rollback + 15m canary + 30m prod rollout if no regressions. Will update thread.

oncall-bot: @channel INC-3124 status: workaround in progress. Follow-up actions logged in INC ticket.

lina: added a short summary for customer: "We've identified a control-plane header precedence regression that caused tenant-level tier headers to be ignored when a global tier header was present. We're rolling back the change and will monitor traffic; we'll follow up with timeline and logs once resolved." :thumbsup:

devon: postmortem items already noted: add e2e test for mixed-tier headers, add telemetry to count mixed-header collisions, improve docs on header precedence.

maya: rollback complete to prod, canary looked clean. Please monitor acme metrics and paste any failing request ids here.

qa-sam: verified acme's test traffic after rollback — selected_pool=gold-dedicated-01 for rq_8a1f2-replay. No 429s observed in the next 10m sample.

alex: confirmed — errors stopped ~12:03 UTC. Thank you team.

lina: closing loop with customer, will keep INC open for follow-up verification and to track the regression fix in main branch.

devon: adding labels: root_cause=controlplane-tier-precedence, impact=dedicated-throttle, mitigation=rollback, followup=tests+telemetry

maya: follow-up PR (CP-4489) created to add explicit precedence and regression test.

lina: great work everyone.
